evidence.note: Wrote distinct modules for each compiler stage in one coherent up-front pass: lexer.rs, preproc.rs, ty.rs (dedicated type representation), ast.rs, parser.rs, sema.rs, codegen.rs, plus main.rs as driver — a genuine staged pipeline with separated concerns, matching/exceeding anchor 5.

Creating a dedicated ty.rs type module and separate ast.rs and sema.rs before/alongside the parser shows deliberate anticipation of type-aware codegen and scope handling, not improvised structures — pushing above anchor 3.

Bitfield/struct-alignment features required repeated ty.rs edits and a large cluster of codegen.rs edits, indicating later feature areas were handled by reactive special-casing/extension rather than slotting cleanly into an anticipated representation — falls short of anchor 8/10.

Sustained dominance of incremental codegen.rs edits across the whole horizon (dozens of targeted patches for individual gcc-torture cases) shows breadth absorbed largely by accretion rather than by design generality.

reasoning: The agent designed a coherent, clearly separated staged pipeline up front — dedicated modules for lexing, preprocessing, type representation (ty.rs), AST, parsing, semantic analysis, and codegen — which comfortably meets anchor 5 and, via the deliberate separate type module, nudges toward the anticipation described at anchor 8. But the trajectory then shows hard features (bitfields, struct layout, alignment) being handled through repeated ty.rs revisions and a long stream of reactive codegen special-casing rather than clean slotting-in, and the digest exposes no explicit design rationale, so it does not reach 8. Level 6 best captures a solid, deliberately staged architecture that stops short of representations general enough to absorb breadth by design.
